text: 'If Γ ⊨ φ then Γ ⊢ φ' states which property, and what does it assert informally?
choices: Soundness — the proof system never proves falsehoods
Consistency — no formula and its negation are both provable
Completeness — everything that is semantically forced is provable
Decidability — there is an algorithm deciding provability
explanation: Completeness is the direction ⊨ ⟹ ⊢: whatever is true in all models is provable. Soundness (option 1) is the converse ⊢ ⟹ ⊨. Consistency (option 2) and decidability (option 4) are entirely different properties.
